```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  collapse = TRUE,
  comment = "#>"
)
# numDeriv (numeric-Jacobian demo) and boot (bootstrap comparison, echo-only
# chunks) are optional Suggests; guard the chunks that need them so the
# vignette knits whether or not they are installed.
have_numderiv <- requireNamespace("numDeriv", quietly = TRUE)
have_boot     <- requireNamespace("boot", quietly = TRUE)
```

## Two sources of uncertainty

2S-PA accounts for **measurement error in factor scores** by fixing score
loadings and error variances in stage 2. Those fixed quantities are themselves
estimated in stage 1, however, and can vary from sample to sample.
The default stage-2 standard errors condition on them as if they were known.

This vignette illustrates an additional, first-order delta-method correction
to the **sampling standard errors of the structural parameter estimates**.
The correction adds uncertainty associated with the estimated score loadings
and error covariance matrix. It changes the reported standard errors and
confidence intervals, while leaving the path estimates unchanged. Related
two-step corrections are discussed by
[Meijer et al. (2021)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00181-020-01942-z).

### A short example

```{r load-pkg, message=FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(R2spa)
if (have_numderiv) library(numDeriv)
if (have_boot) library(boot)
```

For scores from a multi-factor CFA, request `vfsLT = TRUE` in stage 1.
This stores an estimated sampling covariance matrix for the score loadings
and error variances/covariances. Supply that matrix to `tspa()` and request
`corrected_se = TRUE`:

```{r}
measurement_fit <- cfa('ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
                       dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4',
                       data = PoliticalDemocracy)
scores <- get_fs(measurement_fit, vfsLT = TRUE)
fit_plain <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", data = scores)
fit_corrected <- tspa("dem60 ~ ind60", data = scores,
                      vfsLT = attr(scores, "vfsLT"), corrected_se = TRUE)
standardizedSolution(fit_plain) |>
  subset(op == "~")
standardizedSolution(fit_corrected) |>
  subset(op == "~")
```

The correction implemented here propagates uncertainty in `fsL` and `fsT`,
holding the observed score values and score intercepts (`fsb`) fixed.
It omits cross-covariance terms between the two stages. It is therefore a
partial approximation to stage-1 estimation uncertainty, rather than a
complete two-stage sampling variance calculation. A bootstrap that repeats
both stages provides another way to examine uncertainty; an example appears
below.

The numerical derivative demonstrations require `numDeriv`, and the
bootstrap code requires `boot`. The remaining sections explain the
calculation and its use with separate measurement models, Bartlett scores,
and multiple groups.

## How the first-order correction is computed

$$\hat V_{\gamma, c} = \hat V_{\gamma} + \boldsymbol{J}_\boldsymbol{\gamma}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}}) \hat V_{\theta} \boldsymbol{J}_\boldsymbol{\gamma}(\hat{\boldsymbol{\theta}})^\top,$$

where $\hat V_{\gamma}$ is the default covariance matrix of the stage-2
parameter estimates, $\hat V_{\theta}$ is the sampling covariance of the
stage-1 score measurement parameters (`vfsLT`), and
$\boldsymbol{J}_{\boldsymbol{\gamma}}$ describes how the stage-2 estimates
change as those measurement parameters change. The added term translates
stage-1 uncertainty into uncertainty in the structural estimates.

The default calculation uses $\mathbf{J} = -\mathbf{H}^{-1}\mathbf{C}$,
where $\mathbf{H}$ is the stage-2 log-likelihood Hessian and $\mathbf{C}$
contains its cross-derivatives with respect to the fixed score measurement
parameters. Rows of $\mathbf{J}$ correspond to stage-2 parameters and columns
to stage-1 score measurement parameters.

This example is based on the `PoliticalDemocracy` dataset, from the lavaan tutorial (<https://lavaan.ugent.be/tutorial/sem.html>), also used as an example in Bollen (1989).

## Separate Measurement Models

```{r}
model <- '
  # latent variable definitions
     ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
     dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4

  # regressions
    dem60 ~ ind60
'
```

```{r}
cfa_ind60 <- cfa("ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3", data = PoliticalDemocracy)
# Regression factor scores
fs1 <- get_fs(cfa_ind60, vfsLT = TRUE, format = "list")
# Delta method variance of (loading, error variance)
vldev1 <- attr(fs1, which = "vfsLT")
cfa_dem60 <- cfa("dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4",
                 data = PoliticalDemocracy)
# Regression factor scores
fs2 <- get_fs(cfa_dem60, vfsLT = TRUE, format = "list")
# Delta method variance of (loading, error variance)
vldev2 <- attr(fs2, which = "vfsLT")
fs_dat <- data.frame(
  fs_ind60 = fs1$fs_ind60,
  fs_dem60 = fs2$fs_dem60
)
# Combine sampling variance of loading and error variance
# Note: loadings first, then error variance
vldev <- block_diag(vldev1, vldev2)[c(1, 3, 2, 4), c(1, 3, 2, 4)]
```

The two CFAs use the same participants, so their measurement parameter
estimates can be correlated across repeated samples. `block_diag()` sets
that cross-model sampling covariance to zero. The calculation below makes
this simplifying approximation. A multi-factor measurement model estimates
the cross-model covariance as part of a single `vfsLT` matrix.

```{r}
# 2S-PA
# Assemble loadings
ld <- block_diag(attr(fs1, which = "fsL"),
                 attr(fs2, which = "fsL"))
ev <- block_diag(attr(fs1, which = "fsT"),
                 attr(fs2, which = "fsT"))
tspa_fit <- tspa(model = "dem60 ~ ind60",
                 data = fs_dat,
                 fsL = ld,
                 fsT = ev)
# Unadjusted covariance
vcov(tspa_fit)
# Adjusted covariance matrix
(vc_cor <- vcov_corrected(tspa_fit, vfsLT = vldev, which_free = c(1, 4, 5, 7)))
# Corrected standard errors
sqrt(diag(vc_cor))
```

`vcov_corrected()` returns the corrected covariance matrix without changing
the fit. The alternative `tspa(corrected_se = TRUE)` stores that matrix in
the returned lavaan fit, so functions such as `standardizedSolution()` use it.

For technical comparisons, `engine = "analytic"` uses derivatives of the
likelihood score without refitting the model. `engine = "fd"` perturbs the
measurement parameters and refits stage 2 to approximate the derivatives.
The latter is also used as a fallback when the default calculation does not
support the fitted model.

For the one-call option, `which_free` identifies the measurement quantities
whose uncertainty is being propagated. In this separate-model example,
positions 1 and 4 are the two score loadings and positions 5 and 7 are the
two error variances. Their order must match the rows and columns of `vldev`:

```{r}
tspa_fit_corr <- tspa(model = "dem60 ~ ind60",
                      data = fs_dat,
                      fsL = ld,
                      fsT = ev,
                      vfsLT = vldev,
                      which_free = c(1, 4, 5, 7),
                       corrected_se = TRUE)
keep_dem_ind <- function(std) {
  std[std$lhs == "dem60" & std$rhs == "ind60" & std$op == "~", , drop = FALSE]
}
sc <- keep_dem_ind(standardizedSolution(tspa_fit_corr))
sc$est.std              # unchanged point estimate
sc$se                   # corrected standard SE (matches the hand-derived value)
attr(tspa_fit_corr, "tspa_corrected")   # TRUE
```

### Comparison with joint SEM

For comparison, obtain the standard errors of the corresponding
unstandardized parameters from a joint SEM:

```{r}
sem_fit <- sem(model, data = PoliticalDemocracy)
# Covariance of the structural parameter estimates
(vc_j <- 
  vcov(sem_fit)[c("dem60~ind60", "ind60~~ind60", "dem60~~dem60"),
                c("dem60~ind60", "ind60~~ind60", "dem60~~dem60")])
sqrt(diag(vc_j))
```

### Bootstrap standard errors

Resample participants and repeat both stages in each bootstrap sample.
The code below shows the procedure; this vignette reads stored bootstrap
results rather than running 1,999 replications each time it is built.

```{r, eval = FALSE, echo = TRUE}
run_tspa <- function(df, inds) {
  # local = TRUE: score each latent from its own (separate) measurement model
  fs_dat <- get_fs(object = df[inds, ],
                   model = "ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
                            dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4",
                   local = TRUE,
                   se = "none", test = "none")
  # tspa() reads fsL/fsT/fsb and the per-score SEs from the get_fs() result
  tspa_fit <- tspa(model = "dem60 ~ ind60",
                   data = fs_dat,
                   test = "none")
  coef(tspa_fit)
}
boo <- boot(PoliticalDemocracy, statistic = run_tspa, R = 1999)
```

```{r, eval = FALSE, include = FALSE}
saveRDS(boo, file = "boo_separate.RDS")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
boo <- readRDS("boo_separate.RDS")
```

```{r}
# Use MAD to downweigh outlying replications
boo$t |>
    apply(MARGIN = 2, FUN = mad) |>
    setNames(c("dem60~ind60", "ind60~~ind60", "dem60~~dem60"))
```

The displayed bootstrap summary uses the median absolute deviation (MAD),
a robust measure of spread that limits the influence of extreme replications.
The usual bootstrap SE is the standard deviation of the bootstrap estimates.
Neither summary is expected to match the delta-method SE exactly. Joint SEM
and 2S-PA also use different estimators, so their sampling standard errors
need not agree.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
run_sem <- function(df, inds) {
  sem_fit <- sem(model, data = df[inds, ], se = "none", test = "none")
  coef(sem_fit)
}
boo <- boot(PoliticalDemocracy, statistic = run_sem, R = 999)
```

### With Bartlett's Method

```{r}
# Factor score
fsb_joint <- get_fs(PoliticalDemocracy,
                    model = "ind60 =~ x1 + x2 + x3
                             dem60 =~ y1 + y2 + y3 + y4",
                    method = "Bartlett",
                    vfsLT = TRUE)
vldevb_joint <- attr(fsb_joint, which = "vfsLT")
```

```{r}
tspa_fit2b <- tspa(model = "dem60 ~ ind60",
                   data = fsb_joint,
                   fsT = attr(fsb_joint, "fsT"),
                   fsL = diag(2) |>
                       `dimnames<-`(list(c("fs_ind60", "fs_dem60"),
                                         c("ind60", "dem60"))))
# Unadjusted covariance matrix
vcov(tspa_fit2b)
# Adjusted covariance matrix
(vc2b_cor <- vcov_corrected(
    tspa_fit2b,
    # With Bartlett scoring the loadings are fixed, so propagate the error
    # variances only (positions 5 and 7)
    vfsLT = vldevb_joint[c(5, 7), c(5, 7)],
    which_free = c(5, 7)))
# Corrected standard errors
sqrt(diag(vc2b_cor))
```

## Multiple Groups

```{r}
# Multigroup, three-factor example
mod <- "
  # latent variables
    visual =~ x1 + x2 + x3
    textual =~ x4 + x5 + x6
    speed =~ x7 + x8 + x9
"
# Factor scores based on partial invariance
fit <- cfa(mod,
           data = HolzingerSwineford1939,
           std.lv = TRUE,
           group = "school",
           group.equal = c("loadings", "intercepts"),
           group.partial = c("visual=~x2", "x7~1"))
fs_dat <- get_fs_lavaan(fit, vfsLT = TRUE)
vldev <- attr(fs_dat, which = "vfsLT")
```

```{r}
tspa_fit <- tspa(model = "visual ~~ textual + speed
                          textual ~~ speed",
                 data = fs_dat,
                 group = "school",
                 fsL = attr(fs_dat, which = "fsL"),
                 fsT = attr(fs_dat, which = "fsT"))
# Unadjusted covariance of the structural parameters (the 12 factor
# variances/covariances, 6 per group); the 6 factor-score intercepts (fs_*~1)
# are omitted.
keep <- grepl("~~", rownames(vcov(tspa_fit)))
vcov(tspa_fit)[keep, keep]
# Adjusted covariance
vcov_corrected(tspa_fit, vfsLT = vldev)[keep, keep]
```

The correction can be requested in place on `tspa()`, so `vcov()` (and hence the SEs derived from it) and `standardizedSolution()` on the returned fit report the corrected standard errors (the point estimates are unchanged):

```{r}
tspa_fit_corr <- tspa(model = "visual ~~ textual + speed
                               textual ~~ speed",
                      data = fs_dat,
                      group = "school",
                      fsL = attr(fs_dat, which = "fsL"),
                      fsT = attr(fs_dat, which = "fsT"),
                      vfsLT = vldev,
                      corrected_se = TRUE)
attr(tspa_fit_corr, "tspa_corrected")   # TRUE
round(cbind(unadjusted = sqrt(diag(vcov(tspa_fit))),
            corrected    = sqrt(diag(vcov(tspa_fit_corr)))), 4)
```

### Corrected grand-standardized solution (multigroup)

`grand_standardized_solution()` expresses each group's paths in grand-SD
units for the combined sample. This differs from the within-group SD units
used by `standardizedSolution()`. The function also accepts its original
name, `grandStandardizedSolution()`, used below. When given the corrected
fit, it uses the corrected covariance matrix to obtain standard errors:

```{r}
path_mg <- "textual ~ visual + speed
            visual  ~ speed"
tspa_path  <- tspa(path_mg, data = fs_dat, group = "school",
                   fsL = attr(fs_dat, "fsL"), fsT = attr(fs_dat, "fsT"))
tspa_path_corr <- tspa(path_mg, data = fs_dat, group = "school",
                       fsL = attr(fs_dat, "fsL"), fsT = attr(fs_dat, "fsT"),
                       vfsLT = vldev, corrected_se = TRUE)
gr0 <- grandStandardizedSolution(tspa_path)       # uncorrected
gr1 <- grandStandardizedSolution(tspa_path_corr)  # corrected (SE only)
keep <- gr1$op == "~"
round(cbind(grand_std = gr1$est.std[keep],
            se_plain  = gr0$se[keep],
            se_corr   = gr1$se[keep]), 4)
# SE-only: identical point estimates, corrected SEs >= uncorrected
all(gr1$est.std[keep] == gr0$est.std[keep])
all(gr1$se[keep] >= gr0$se[keep])
```


```{r}
keep_dem_ind <- function(std) {
  std[std$lhs %in% c("visual", "textual", "speed") &
    std$rhs %in% c("visual", "textual", "speed") & 
      std$lhs != std$rhs, , drop = FALSE]
}
tspa_est_std <- function(ld_ev) {
  fsL1 <- attr(fs_dat, which = "fsL")
  fsT1 <- attr(fs_dat, which = "fsT")
  fsL1[[1]][] <- ld_ev[1:9]
  fsL1[[2]][] <- ld_ev[10:18]
  fsT1[[1]][] <- ld_ev[c(19:21, 20, 22:23, 21, 23, 24)]
  fsT1[[2]][] <- ld_ev[c(25:27, 26, 28:29, 27, 29, 30)]
  tfit <- tspa(model = "visual ~~ textual + speed
                        textual ~~ speed",
               data = fs_dat,
               group = "school",
               fsL = fsL1,
               fsT = fsT1) 
  keep_dem_ind(standardizedSolution(tfit))$est.std
}
ld_ev0 <- c(attr(fs_dat, which = "fsL")[[1]],
            attr(fs_dat, which = "fsL")[[2]],
            attr(fs_dat, which = "fsT")[[1]][c(1:3, 5:6, 9)],
            attr(fs_dat, which = "fsT")[[2]][c(1:3, 5:6, 9)])
tspa_est_std(ld_ev0)
```

The following calculation expresses the added variance from stage 1
relative to the default variance of the standardized estimates. It requires
`numDeriv`:

```{r, eval = have_numderiv}
jac <- numDeriv::jacobian(tspa_est_std, x = ld_ev0)
v0 <- lavInspect(tspa_fit, "vcov.std.lv")[c(1:3, 10:12), c(1:3, 10:12)]
sqrt(diag(jac %*% vldev %*% t(jac)) / diag(v0))
```
